body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that, for every growth array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), every interior realized path \(z_0\), and every exact design array with \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for all \(s\),
\[
c\left(\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}\vee N^{-\lambda}\right)
\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\le CR_D.
\]
For the repaired anchor search, \(\Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0,(X_{st}))=0\) on these design arrays. No two-sided conditional lower bound by the entire \(R_D\) is asserted: Gram coercivity alone does not make its realized-design term an optimal-recovery lower bound.
body.justification: The repaired theorem gives a feasible conditional oracle upper bound and sharp treated and donor lower channels in the early-kill regime.
body.gap: The realized Gram radius is not itself a fixed-design optimal-recovery lower bound, so a two-sided conditional \(R_D\) equivalence is not claimed.
body.consumer: The marginal theorem averages the oracle bound and obtains sharpness from random-design occupancy.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.
\]
By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, consistency and event-date transport imply the observed-law equality
\[
\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus (1) is proved from the causal target and is not used as its definition.

We first prove the upper bound. Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), one has \(\kappa=\lambda\), and the integer-order convention gives \(r=0\). Every nonfallback intercept is consequently a convex combination of the replicated means \(\overline Q_{st}\). Fix a design with \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\). By the corrected definition of \(g_{sT}\), the pair \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) belongs to every \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\). Hence \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\ne\varnothing\), so \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) is impossible conditional on this design. Optimality of the selected certificate gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda+C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda+C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
&\qquad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda+C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda+C_V(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The bandwidth floor gives
\[
(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda.
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression}, the support of \(K\), and (2)--(3) imply
\[
|\mathbb E(\widehat m_{s\ell}\mid z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j))-m_s(z_{0s})|
\le C\{\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+(h_s^\star)^\lambda\}.
\tag{4}
\]
The terms in (4) are, respectively, selected-anchor extrapolation, the within-kernel Holder increment, and the increment from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\). Clipping cannot enlarge this error because the reference mean lies in \([-B,B]\).

Let \(m_\ell=|I_\ell|\). Balanced splitting gives \(m_\ell\ge N/3\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), while donor unbiasedness and conditional independence give
\[
\mathbb E\{\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\mid z_0\}
\le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{m_\ell}\le\frac{3SdC_\Sigma}{N}.
\]
Jensen's inequality therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E\{\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^{2\lambda}\mid z_0\}\le(3SdC_\Sigma/N)^\lambda.
\tag{5}
\]

Average the foldwise convex weights and denote the result by \(w_{st}\). Conditional on \(z_0,(X_{st})\), and the donors, define
\[
U_{si}=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)-\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}.
\]
Design-conditional centering gives \(\mathbb E(U_{si}\mid z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j))=0\). Donor--panel separation and conditional cross-unit independence make the \(U_{si}\) independent across \((s,i)\). Since \(\sum_t w_{st}=1\), bounded wealth gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\). Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}\mathrel{\Big|}z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j)\right)\le16B^2A.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (4)--(6), using fixed \(S\), and averaging over donors yields
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
\le C\left[A+N^{-\lambda}+\left\{\sum_s\pi_s(h_s^\star)^\lambda\right\}^2\right]\le CR_D.
\tag{7}
\]

For the treated-mean converse, fix a bounded regression surface satisfying the disclosed modulus with slack, take \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), and keep the design and donor laws fixed. Put \(b\in(0,B]\), and under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\) let independently
\[
\Pr_v\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\}=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
\qquad
\varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\]
For small fixed \(\gamma\), all probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\), consistency and both centering equalities hold, and the targets are separated by
\[
\Delta=4b\sum_s\pi_s\varepsilon_s=4\gamma\sqrt A.
\tag{8}
\]
Their Hellinger affinity is
\[
\prod_s(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}\ge\exp(-8\gamma^2/b^2),
\]
using \(\log(1-x)\ge-2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\). Cauchy--Schwarz bounds total variation strictly below one. Assigning any estimator to the nearer target and integrating the smaller density gives
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\ge cA.
\tag{9}
\]
Under the displayed compatibility condition, \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives target separation at least \(c_0N^{-\lambda/2}\) and total variation bounded away from one. The same nearer-target test gives
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\ge cN^{-\lambda}.
\tag{10}
\]
Taking the larger of (9) and (10) proves the lower bound. Equations (2)--(7) prove the upper bound without any temporal independence within a unit.
